headline: Jio IPO booked over 3 times on day one as oil tops 110 dollars

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Thursday, the twenty-second of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, the Jio Platforms share sale got off to a flying start. It was fully subscribed within about 100 minutes, and ended day one booked more than three times over.

Second, the Reserve Bank's tone has hardened. Minutes of its policy meeting, where all six members voted to raise the repo rate by a quarter point to 5.5 percent, show inflation is spreading. Nomura now expects another hike in December.

And third, oil is back above 110 dollars a barrel after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and Indian shares are set for a weak start.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
To the last session, on Wednesday. It was a day of wild swings. The Sensex rallied in early trade, then fell about 1,400 points from its high before late buying trimmed the damage. It closed down 143 points. The Nifty lost about 78 points to end at 22,811, just holding the 22,800 mark.

The real pain was in the broader market. The Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices each fell more than 2 percent, and the Economic Times says midcaps have now entered correction territory. Around 8 lakh crore rupees of market value was wiped out. Defence stocks fell about 3 percent, and gold lenders such as Manappuram and IIFL Finance dropped up to 6 percent as gold hit a one-week low.

On the other side, IT stocks added about 77,000 crore rupees in value, while banks and financials lost around 81,000 crore rupees as bond yields climbed. The 10-year government bond yield closed at 7.44 percent, its highest since November 2022. The Reserve Bank also rejected all bids at a Treasury bill auction as short-term yields surged.

Foreign institutional investors were net buyers, at around 1,022 crore rupees. Domestic institutions bought about 1,614 crore rupees.

This morning, GIFT Nifty was around 22,682, pointing to a negative open, and Asian markets are lower. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see support at 22,800 to 22,700, and say a close below that could open the way to 22,500. On the upside, 23,000 is the level to reclaim, with Monday's high of 23,175 a key resistance. The volatility index is at a four-month high.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the Jio offer. The 30,213 crore rupee issue was fully subscribed in about 100 minutes, the fastest of India's mega issues. By the close it was booked 3.16 times. Large institutions bid for more than nine times their quota and non-institutional investors 1.68 times, but retail investors only 0.73 times. The Economic Times puts day one bids at around 70,000 crore rupees, ahead of the LIC and NSE issues. Mint reports a grey market premium that suggests listing gains of about 22 percent, though grey market prices are unofficial. The offer closes tomorrow, with listing expected on the twenty-eighth.

Also open until tomorrow is Paras Healthcare, which had a muted start at 0.15 times on day one. Analysts quoted by Business Standard say occupancy and execution are the things to watch.

More issues are lined up. Edelweiss's alternatives arm, EAAA India Alternatives, opens a 1,200 crore rupee issue on Monday, the twenty-sixth, at 1,585 to 1,665 rupees a share. SFC Environmental Technologies, a wastewater treatment firm, opens a 668 crore rupee issue on the twenty-seventh, at 313 to 330 rupees.

On deals, Persistent Systems has launched a qualified institutional placement of up to 4,265 crore rupees, with a floor price of 5,550 rupees a share. And the Economic Times reports that banks are now funding takeovers worth over 10,000 crore rupees after the Reserve Bank eased acquisition finance rules, with State Bank of India and others lending up to 75 percent of deal values.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
To results. Among lenders, Mahindra Finance's September quarter profit jumped 55 percent to 882 crore rupees, on higher volumes and lower credit costs. Its business assets grew 15 percent to 1.47 lakh crore rupees. Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC went the other way, with profit down 8.4 percent to 221 crore rupees as expenses rose 21 percent.

In consumer businesses, PC Jeweller's profit rose 58 percent to 331 crore rupees, on sales of about 1,054 crore rupees, and the company says it is now debt-free after repaying its banks early. Indian Hotels, the Tata group's hotel company, grew profit 19 percent to about 380 crore rupees, on revenue of about 2,484 crore rupees. Vishal Mega Mart's profit rose just 3.7 percent to about 158 crore rupees, and the stock fell 6 percent as the shift in the festive season squeezed margins. Just Dial's profit fell nearly 10 percent to about 108 crore rupees, and its shares slid 6 percent.

In cement, UltraTech's profit rose 21 percent to about 1,494 crore rupees. Jefferies says a recovery in cement prices is the key trigger. Eternal also reported strong growth in revenue and profit.

Today's list is long. Swiggy, Hindustan Petroleum, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Total Gas and Colgate-Palmolive India are among more than 50 companies reporting.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now the economy, and the Reserve Bank. Minutes of the policy committee show inflation is top of mind. Governor Sanjay Malhotra spoke of a generalisation of inflation, with many items running above 4 percent. He said the length and extent of the rate hike cycle will depend on how growth and inflation develop. The Reserve Bank has raised its growth forecast for this financial year to 7.1 percent, from 6.7 percent. Nomura expects another quarter point hike in December. And former governor C Rangarajan told Moneycontrol that with both inflation and the rupee under pressure, the degree of tightening may have to be higher.

On the data, core sector output grew 7.9 percent in September, a 30-month high, led by a sharp rebound in coal and higher iron ore and refinery output. But oil is weighing on the import bill. India's crude imports cost 90.6 billion dollars between April and September, up 46 percent, and the Indian crude basket has averaged about 121 dollars a barrel in October.

On trade, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal heads to Germany and the Netherlands, with the India and European Union trade talks on the agenda.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil again. Brent rose about 1.2 percent to around 110 dollars a barrel, and US crude to about 98 dollars, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia killed three people. Washington has ordered some diplomats' families to leave. At home, Indian Oil plans to buy less West Asian crude under its annual deals.

On Wall Street, stocks rose on strong AI-linked earnings. The Nasdaq gained more than 1 percent, and SpaceX jumped 7 percent on its results and talk of a merger with Tesla. The US 10-year yield is around 5.12 percent, and France's 10-year yield has hit 5 percent. The Federal Reserve meets on the twenty-eighth.

Asia is weaker this morning. Asian shares fell about 0.8 percent, with South Korea's Kospi down nearly 2 percent on worries over AI spending. China's main index is on the edge of a bear market, down about 20 percent from its June high.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script:
An update on the Jio IPO you're following. It was fully subscribed in about 100 minutes and booked 3.16 times on day one, but retail investors have yet to fill their quota.

And on the India and US trade deal you're following. Marco Rubio toured Reliance's Jamnagar refinery with Mukesh Ambani, discussing energy, technology and data centres, as his India visit wraps up today.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, starting with tax. Tax audit reports for assessment year 2026-27 were due on the twenty-first of October. Returns for audited taxpayers are due on the twenty-first of November.

If you sold a house and bought another, Mint notes that the capital gains exemption under Section 54, which is Section 82 of the new Income Tax Act, can be denied or withdrawn if its conditions are not met. Mint also points out that large UPI transfers don't by themselves trigger tax notices, but unexplained bank credits can draw scrutiny.

For salaried readers, the EPF wage ceiling is set to rise from 15,000 to 25,000 rupees, which could change take-home pay.

On gold, prices in India have fallen nearly 5 percent in a month. Kaynat Chainwala of Kotak Neo says gold could test 4,000 dollars an ounce if oil extends its rally and lifts inflation.

Two banking alerts. State Bank of India is investigating a suspected dark web leak of customer records, and says its core operations are unaffected. HDFC Bank has begun an internal probe into alleged leaks of confidential information.

One date for your calendar. Today is the last day to buy shares of Tech Mahindra, IRFC, LTM and several others to be eligible for dividends and corporate actions with a record date of tomorrow. Tech Mahindra has also proposed a one-for-one bonus issue.

That's your brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty can hold 22,800 as oil reacts to the Gulf, and whether retail investors step up on day two of the Jio offer. Results from Swiggy and Hindustan Petroleum are due, and bond yields remain the thing to watch for bank stocks. Have a good Thursday.
